newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuban ruling party to hold policy-making congress.
newsitem.headline: Cuban ruling party to hold policy-making congress.

text.p: Cuba's ruling Communist Party will hold a policy-making congress to map out economic and political strategies for the nation in the years to come, an official Cuban newspaper said Tuesday.
The Communist Party daily Granma did not specify a date for the Fifth Party Congress but Cuban officials say it is expected to be held in the last months of this year, probably October.
The last party congress, the fourth, was held in October 1991.

Granma said the decision to hold a congress, which elects the leadership of the ruling party and defines national policies, was made at a meeting of the party Central Committee presided over by its leader, Cuban President Fidel Castro.

The dates of the fifth congress are expected to be announced on Wednesday during celebrations to mark the 36th anniversary of the day Castro declared the Cuban Revolution would follow a socialist course.
The Central Committee meeting last weekend also heard a report on the economy by Vice-President Carlos Lage.

Granma said Lage focused on the main challenges facing the Cuban economy, which is still fighting to shake off the effects of a five-year recession triggered by the collapse of the island's trade and aid ties with the former Soviet bloc.

Lage stressed those economic tasks in which "greater effort" was required, the newspaper added. One of these was believed to be the current sugar harvest, where problems and delays have been reported.

Granma said that Castro closed the Central Committee meeting with a speech in which he stressed the importance of holding the party congress at a time when Cuba was facing "challenges and attacks" -- an apparent reference to the tightened U.S. economic embargo against the island.

Castro referred to the capacity of the Cuban people to "be more efficient, maintain their heroic resistance and keep on advancing in the struggle to preserve their sovereignty, their history and the conquests of Socialism," the newspaper said.
